title: Numerical data and code for A comparative valuation of digital assets through text representation and predictive models in the non-fungible token market
description:
Data and code accompanying the manuscript A comparative valuation of digital assets through text representation and predictive models in the non-fungible token market, submitted to PeerJ Computer Science as an AI Application.

The package includes collection metadata, derived modeling inputs for 8,850 tokens, frozen feature matrices, fixed split identifiers, analysis and verification code, configurations, predictions, scores, and documentation for 40 representation/predictor configurations. Numerical inputs and results are unchanged from the peerj-20261002 baseline. This version adds revised documentation, author-provided SQL for Azuki transaction retrieval, citation information, and author-approved licensing.

The original Dune transaction CSV and pretrained model weights are excluded. The SQL is provided for data access and was not re-executed for this release; it does not guarantee reconstruction of the exact historical export. Reproduction starts from the supplied derived inputs.

Licenses: author-written code: MIT (https://opensource.org/license/mit); author-owned derived data and documentation: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). These licenses apply to separate file categories, as specified in LICENSE.txt. Third-party collection metadata and underlying third-party rights are excluded from the grants. The record's Other (Open) label denotes these mixed terms, not a new blanket license.
